question: Name the water-soluble form of bilirubin created during phototherapy that is easily excreted by the baby.

options.A: Albumin
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Biliverdin
options.D: Lumirubin

explanation: Light converts toxic fat-soluble bilirubin into lumirubin, which dissolves in water and leaves the body through urine and stool. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T7#BMP220_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why is atropine sometimes given before surgery and anesthesia?

options.A: To relax all the skeletal muscles fully
options.B: To put the patient into a deep sleep
options.C: To prevent sudden postpartum bleeding
options.D: To reduce respiratory and oral secretions

explanation: Drying up airway and salivary secretions prevents the patient from choking or aspirating mucus while under anesthesia. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T5#BMP124_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which government body typically oversees the administration of public secondary health facilities in Nigerian states?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Education
options.B: Local Primary Health Care Authority
options.C: Hospital Management Board
options.D: National Universities Commission

explanation: State Hospital Management Boards or Ministries of Health hold the direct administrative responsibility for public General Hospitals. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which behavior shows an avoidance symptom in a mother with postpartum PTSD?

options.A: Constantly talking about every single detail of her difficult labor
options.B: Attending all scheduled postnatal immunization appointments early
options.C: Checking the baby's breathing every two minutes throughout the night
options.D: Refusing to walk past the hospital where she delivered her baby

explanation: Avoidance means staying away from places, people, or reminders that bring back painful memories of a traumatic birth. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T4#BMP223_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why must chemical cleaning agents be stored completely away from food preparation areas?

options.A: To keep the kitchen counters looking neat and organized
options.B: To stop the cleaning liquids from evaporating too quickly
options.C: To ensure the staff can find cooking ingredients faster
options.D: To prevent accidental chemical contamination of edible items

explanation: Storing chemicals near food creates a serious risk of accidental poisoning if the substances leak or get mixed up with ingredients. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T5#BMP117_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which specific part of the nervous system does the poliovirus attack to cause paralysis?

options.A: Sensory nerve endings in the skin
options.B: Cerebellar tissue controlling balance
options.C: Anterior horn cells of the spinal cord
options.D: The myelin sheath of peripheral nerves

explanation: The virus specifically targets motor neurons located in the anterior horn of the spinal cord. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T8#BMP222_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which of the following physical findings is typically observed in a patient experiencing early shock?

options.A: Flushed, warm, and dry skin
options.B: Cool, pale, and clammy skin
options.C: Bounding and very strong pulse
options.D: Slow and deep respiratory pattern

explanation: Peripheral vasoconstriction shunts blood away from the skin, making it feel cool, pale, and clammy. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T4#BMP110_U7_T4_h4)

question: What happens when an OP baby fails to complete its long internal rotation inside the pelvis?

options.A: Deep transverse arrest
options.B: Placental abruption
options.C: Spontaneous fast delivery
options.D: Immediate shoulder dystocia

explanation: If the head stops turning and gets stuck sideways in the mid-pelvis, it is known as a deep transverse arrest requiring professional intervention. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T1#BMP311_U1_T1_h4)

question: A midwife visits a new mother twenty-four hours after a home delivery and finds the baby feels cold to the touch and is breathing rapidly. What should the midwife do FIRST?

options.A: Apply methylated spirit directly to the infant's umbilical cord
options.B: Institute immediate skin-to-skin contact and check environmental warmth
options.C: Advise the mother to start formula milk immediately
options.D: Refer the baby to a tertiary hospital for surgical intervention

explanation: Warming the baby through skin-to-skin contact addresses hypothermia quickly, which is a major danger for newborns. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T2#BMP227_U1_T2_h2)

question: A midwife prepares the wrong dose of oxytocin, but a colleague checks the calculation and stops administration just in time. How should this be classified?

options.A: An adverse event
options.B: A near miss
options.C: A sentinel event
options.D: A normal variance

explanation: Since the medication was stopped before reaching the patient, no harm occurred, making it a classic near miss event. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h2)

question: A midwife assesses a pregnant woman in labor and notes that the lower uterine segment has thinned out. Which anatomical landmark formed this segment?

options.A: Cervix
options.B: Isthmus
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Fundus

explanation: The short narrow region called the isthmus stretches and thins remarkably during late pregnancy and labor to create the lower uterine segment. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T3#BMP210_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which organ serves as the primary site for drug excretion?

options.A: Lungs
options.B: Kidneys
options.C: Skin
options.D: Heart

explanation: The kidneys filter blood and pass water-soluble drug waste out through the urine. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: To prevent pregnancy after unprotected sex
options.B: To terminate an already established pregnancy
options.C: To treat common sexually transmitted infections
options.D: To provide long-term daily birth control

explanation: ECPs are strictly designed as a backup method to prevent fertilization after unprotected intercourse or contraceptive failure, not to end an existing pregnancy. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T10#BMP224_U3_T10_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct effect of high maternal blood glucose on the fetus?

options.A: Excessive deposition of body fat
options.B: Rapid somatic growth
options.C: High glucose levels in fetal blood
options.D: Decreased production of fetal insulin

explanation: High maternal blood sugar actually causes an INCREASE in fetal insulin production, not a decrease. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T3#BMP221_U4_T3_h3)

question: What dangerous habit must midwives avoid when handling used hypodermic needles?

options.A: Carrying them on a kidney dish to the disposal point
options.B: Using a single-handed scoop technique if recapping is required
options.C: Dropping them directly into a nearby puncture-resistant box
options.D: Recapping needles using a traditional two-handed method

explanation: Two-handed recapping is a primary cause of accidental needle-stick injuries because the hand holding the cap is directly in the path of the needle point. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h4)

question: What specific blood pressure reading defines severe hypertension in pregnancy?

options.A: 170/120 mmHg or higher
options.B: 150/100 mmHg or higher
options.C: 160/110 mmHg or higher
options.D: 140/90 mmHg or higher

explanation: Readings reaching 160 over 110 or greater are classified as severe and require immediate medical attention to protect the mother. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T1#BMP221_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which hormone relaxes the stomach muscles and slows down digestion during early pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles throughout the body, including the gastrointestinal tract, which slows digestion and contributes to nausea. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why is family planning typically included in a comprehensive maternal and child health outreach package?

options.A: To support birth spacing and improve overall maternal wellbeing
options.B: To satisfy administrative paperwork requirements for donors
options.C: To replace routine immunization services entirely
options.D: To reduce the total population of children under five years

explanation: Including family planning helps women space their pregnancies safely, which lowers risks for both mothers and babies. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h3)

question: A client reports experiencing severe migraine headaches with aura. Why is gathering this medical history vital for family planning?

options.A: It helps the midwife avoid prescribing estrogen-containing contraceptives due to stroke risks
options.B: It proves the client is suffering from chronic high blood pressure
options.C: It indicates that the client is an ideal candidate for combined oral contraceptive pills
options.D: It requires immediate surgical removal of any previously inserted intrauterine devices

explanation: Migraines with aura combined with hormonal contraceptives significantly elevate the risk of stroke. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T2#BMP224_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the term for sending a patient from a primary health clinic to a General Hospital due to a complication?

options.A: Upward referral
options.B: Community outreach
options.C: Downward discharge
options.D: Lateral transfer

explanation: Moving a patient from a lower level of care to a higher, more specialized facility is known as an upward referral. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is a reason a midwife must NOT insert a levonorgestrel IUCD?

options.A: Desire to have more children later
options.B: Mild primary dysmenorrhea
options.C: History of primary school education
options.D: Current confirmed pregnancy

explanation: An IUCD should never be inserted if the client is already pregnant, as it poses serious risks to both the pregnancy and the mother. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T9#BMP224_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which cells in the hypodermis are primarily responsible for storing fat?

options.A: Adipocytes
options.B: Melanocytes
options.C: Keratinocytes
options.D: Fibroblasts

explanation: Adipocytes are specialized cells designed specifically to store energy in the form of neutral fats inside the body. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T3#BMP111_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary driver behind the rapid spread of antimicrobial resistance?

options.A: The natural cooling of environmental temperatures
options.B: Normal human hormonal changes during pregnancy
options.C: Regular intake of sterile drinking water
options.D: Overuse and misuse of antibiotic drugs

explanation: Using antibiotics when they are not needed or failing to finish a full prescription creates an environment where resistant bacteria survive and thrive. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T9#BMP116_U2_T9_h4)

question: In midwifery, when is intravenous hydralazine primarily used?

options.A: Early-onset morning sickness
options.B: Severe gestational hypertension
options.C: Premature rupture of membranes
options.D: Uncomplicated gestational diabetes

explanation: Hydralazine is given when a pregnant woman's blood pressure climbs to dangerously high levels that put her and her baby at risk. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T3#BMP213_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the typical maximum duration for using salbutamol as a tocolytic?

options.A: Nine months
options.B: Two full weeks
options.C: About 48 hours
options.D: Until the end of the first trimester

explanation: Salbutamol is only used short-term (roughly 48 hours) because the body quickly builds a tolerance to its relaxing effects. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which condition is most commonly linked with an exaggerated or jittery Moro response?

options.A: Normal physiological weight loss
options.B: Transient newborn skin rashes
options.C: Physiological jaundice of the newborn
options.D: Neonatal abstinence syndrome

explanation: Withdrawal from substances or extreme irritability can make the nervous system overreact, causing jittery and exaggerated reflexes. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T3#BMP214_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is grey literature?

options.A: Confidential patient hospital files kept in the medical records room
options.B: Outdated medical textbooks older than twenty years in a library
options.C: Reports and documents published outside traditional commercial academic journals
options.D: Academic research papers that have been rejected by peer reviewers

explanation: Grey literature includes government reports, conference papers, and policy briefs not managed by commercial publishers. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T1#BMP225_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which specific register should a midwife use to record intrapartum details and birth weights?

options.A: Maternity and Delivery Register
options.B: Daily Outpatient Attendance Register
options.C: Antenatal Care Register
options.D: Child Health and Immunization Register

explanation: The maternity and delivery register is specifically designed to capture events that happen during labor, childbirth, and the immediate postnatal period. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h2)

question: Where are irregular bones mostly found in the human body?

options.A: Exclusively inside the palms of the hands and soles of feet
options.B: Floating freely within major abdominal muscle walls
options.C: Along the central axis like the spine and skull base
options.D: In the long free-moving structures of the arms and legs

explanation: The central skeleton, particularly the spinal column and the base of the skull, contains most of the body's irregular bones. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T6#BMP111_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why should a child's fingernails be kept trimmed short during a chickenpox infection?

options.A: To stop viral particles from multiplying under the nails
options.B: To make wearing mittens more comfortable
options.C: To prevent skin sores and secondary bacterial infections from scratching
options.D: To help calamine lotion dry faster on the skin

explanation: Short nails help prevent skin damage when the child scratches itchy blisters, lowering the risk of bacteria entering the skin. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T4#BMP222_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is a positive treponemal test result alone not enough to prove a patient has an active, current infection?

options.A: Treponemal antibodies disappear within two weeks of contracting the disease
options.B: Treponemal antibodies usually remain in the blood for life, even after successful treatment
options.C: Treponemal tests frequently give false-positive results in healthy pregnant women
options.D: Treponemal tests only measure acute inflammation rather than the presence of bacteria

explanation: Because treponemal antibodies persist long-term regardless of whether the infection is active or cured, these tests cannot differentiate past treated infections from current ones. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T8#BMP221_U4_T8_h3)

question: Which supplement is recommended for 10 to 14 days during acute childhood diarrhea to shorten illness duration?

options.A: Zinc tablets
options.B: Folic acid
options.C: Iron drops
options.D: Vitamin A

explanation: World Health Organization guidelines recommend daily zinc supplementation during diarrhea to boost immunity and gut repair. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T4#BMP222_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of school health inspections?

options.A: Prescribing major surgical operations for students
options.B: Controlling the spread of communicable diseases
options.C: Detecting nutritional deficiencies early
options.D: Generating local health baseline statistics

explanation: School inspections focus on screening, prevention, and basic health promotion, not major surgical procedures which belong in hospitals. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h2)

question: What temperature range defines the danger zone where bacteria multiply rapidly?

options.A: Between minus 10°C and 0°C
options.B: Between 70°C and 100°C
options.C: Between 15°C and 25°C
options.D: Between 5°C and 60°C

explanation: Bacteria thrive and multiply quickly when perishable food is left within the temperature danger zone of 5°C to 60°C. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T5#BMP117_U4_T5_h2)

question: How does chickenpox usually spread from person to person?

options.A: Through mosquito and insect bites
options.B: Through eating unwashed raw vegetables
options.C: Through respiratory droplets and blister fluid
options.D: Through drinking contaminated water

explanation: The virus travels through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes, or through direct contact with the fluid from active blisters. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T4#BMP222_U2_T4_h1)

question: What are the basic building blocks that make up protein molecules?

options.A: Amino acids
options.B: Nucleic acids
options.C: Fatty acids
options.D: Simple sugars

explanation: Proteins are constructed from long chains of amino acids linked together. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h1)

question: How can high anxiety in a mother negatively affect breastfeeding?

options.A: It releases adrenaline, which can inhibit the oxytocin-driven let-down reflex
options.B: It changes the chemical composition of colostrum into toxic fluid
options.C: It immediately stops the anterior pituitary gland from producing prolactin forever
options.D: It causes the infant to permanently lose its rooting and sucking reflexes

explanation: Stress triggers adrenaline, which gets in the way of oxytocin and makes it harder for milk to flow out. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why does a pregnant woman have a much higher need for tissue-building nutrients?

options.A: To prevent the sudden accumulation of excessive body fat
options.B: To support the growth of the fetus, placenta, and expanded blood volume
options.C: To lower her basal metabolic rate during the third trimester
options.D: To completely stop the normal process of cellular turnover

explanation: Pregnancy involves massive anatomical changes and tissue creation, requiring a steady supply of structural building blocks. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a quick comprehension check during a lecture?

options.A: To identify immediate comprehension gaps among students
options.B: To determine final semester grades and graduation status
options.C: To eliminate the need for any future examinations
options.D: To punish students who arrived late to the classroom

explanation: Formative assessments are quick checks used during a class to see if students understand the topic before moving on. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h8)

question: What type of organism causes trichomoniasis?

options.A: A protozoan parasite
options.B: A gram-negative bacterium
options.C: A double-stranded virus
options.D: A superficial fungus

explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis is a single-celled protozoan that uses flagella to move through genital fluids. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h1)

question: What immediate step should a midwife take right after inserting an implant?

options.A: Administer a booster injection of antibiotics
options.B: Palpate the rod(s) to confirm they are under the skin
options.C: Send the client for an immediate pelvic ultrasound scan
options.D: Instruct the client to avoid lifting any objects for a month

explanation: The midwife must feel the implant immediately after placement to ensure it is correctly positioned and not deeply embedded. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T7#BMP224_U3_T7_h4)

question: At what age is primary amenorrhea investigated if secondary sexual characteristics are completely absent?

options.A: Seventeen years
options.B: Thirteen years
options.C: Fifteen years
options.D: Nineteen years

explanation: If a girl reaches age thirteen without starting her period and also shows no signs of breast development or other pubertal changes, primary amenorrhea is investigated. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h2)

question: What term describes the powdery white deposit of urea sometimes seen on the skin in severe kidney failure?

options.A: Miliaria plaque
options.B: Uremic frost
options.C: Eczema crust
options.D: Seborrheic scale

explanation: Uremic frost occurs when high levels of urea in the blood are excreted through sweat and leave crystals on the skin as moisture evaporates. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T7#BMP111_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why might a patient with angina feel pain spreading to the left arm or jaw?

options.A: Nerve signals from the heart share spinal cord pathways with nerves from the arm and jaw.
options.B: The coronary arteries directly connect to the blood vessels of the upper limbs.
options.C: The heart muscle physically stretches outward until it touches the shoulder joint.
options.D: Lactic acid travels rapidly through the lymphatic system into the facial muscles.

explanation: This is called referred pain because sensory fibers from the heart and upper body enter the same segments of the spinal cord. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T3#BMP125_U2_T3_h4)

question: During a home birth, a mother's pulse rises from 80 to 110 beats per minute alongside a rising temperature. What does this suggest?

options.A: Fetal distress needing an immediate vacuum extraction at home
options.B: An expected response to successful pushing
options.C: Developing maternal fatigue, dehydration, or potential infection
options.D: Normal body adjustment to the transition phase of labor

explanation: A rising pulse and temperature are classic warning signs of fatigue, dehydration, or intrauterine infection requiring close evaluation. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T3#BMP215_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the main job of a spermicide inside the vagina?

options.A: To stop a fertilized egg from implanting
options.B: To permanently thicken the cervical mucus
options.C: To change the natural pH balance of the ovaries
options.D: To immobilize and destroy sperm before they reach the egg

explanation: Spermicides contain chemical agents designed specifically to stop sperm mobility and kill them before they meet the egg. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T3#BMP224_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful strategy for managing unexpected ward absenteeism?

options.A: Using purely punitive measures to scare staff into never falling sick
options.B: Reassessing patient acuity to prioritize critical duties
options.C: Supporting staff facing genuine health or personal crises
options.D: Maintaining a reliable pool of floating or relief staff

explanation: Punishing legitimate illness or crises damages trust and morale, whereas structured relief plans solve the operational problem safely. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T1#BMP312_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which maternal condition makes the use of ergometrine completely unsafe during postpartum haemorrhage management?

options.A: Mild iron deficiency anaemia
options.B: Asymptomatic urinary tract infection
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Severe hypertension or pre-eclampsia

explanation: Ergometrine constricts blood vessels and can dangerously spike blood pressure, making it unsafe for mothers with high blood pressure disorders. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T1#BMP311_U4_T1_h4)

question: A postpartum woman is bleeding profusely from a severe atony. Which action has the highest priority over all others?

options.A: Administering uterotonic drugs and massaging the uterus
options.B: Asking the patient about her medical history
options.C: Completing the birth notification register
options.D: Weighing the soaked linen pads

explanation: Stopping massive hemorrhage is a critical life-saving intervention that must take precedence over paperwork or history gathering. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T9#BMP110_U7_T9_h4)

question: How do hormone signals from the endocrine system generally compare to nerve signals from the nervous system?

options.A: Nervous system actions are permanent whereas hormones are temporary
options.B: Endocrine responses are slower and longer lasting
options.C: Nervous responses rely on circulating chemical messengers
options.D: Endocrine impulses travel exclusively along nerve fibres

explanation: Chemical signals traveling through the blood take longer to start than electrical nerve impulses, but their effects usually last much longer. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h1)

question: What does professional accountability primarily require a midwife to do?

options.A: Work independently without ever consulting doctors
options.B: Take responsibility for her clinical decisions and actions
options.C: Blame assistant staff when labor complications arise
options.D: Follow hospital traditions without questioning them

explanation: Accountability means owning one's clinical choices, acknowledging mistakes, and ensuring safe patient outcomes. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which body changes are linked to protein breakdown in Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Thin skin, muscle wasting in the limbs, and weak bones
options.B: Enlarged calf muscles and thickened epidermal layers
options.C: Increased bone density and enhanced joint cartilage growth
options.D: Rapid healing of surgical incisions and skin wounds

explanation: When cortisol breaks down proteins instead of building them up, it leads to muscle wasting, fragile skin, and weaker bones. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T8#BMP216_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body naturally develop insulin resistance as pregnancy progresses?

options.A: To speed up the digestion of dietary proteins
options.B: To keep more glucose circulating in the blood for the growing fetus
options.C: To prevent the pancreas from producing too much insulin
options.D: To help the mother store more fat in her lower limbs

explanation: Natural insulin resistance makes maternal cells take up less glucose, leaving more available in the bloodstream to cross the placenta to the baby. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h1)

question: A postpartum woman presents with severe shortness of breath two days after a cesarean section. What specific history item is most critical to ask first?

options.A: Frequency of daily fluid intake
options.B: History of seasonal pollen allergies
options.C: Family history of childhood asthma
options.D: Recent long-haul travel or prolonged bed rest

explanation: Postpartum clients face a high risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, especially after surgery or immobility. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T1#BMP125_U1_T1_h2)

question: What was the main goal of establishing the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative globally?

options.A: To replace traditional birth attendants with certified pediatric surgeons
options.B: To stop hospitals from using practices that discourage or disrupt breastfeeding
options.C: To provide free commercial infant formula to every mother giving birth
options.D: To train mothers how to manufacture their own breast milk substitutes

explanation: The initiative targets hospital routines—like unnecessary separation and early formula use—that interfere with successful breastfeeding establishment. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h3)

question: How do school and community programs mainly improve adolescent reproductive health?

options.A: By taking health information and services directly to where youths live and study
options.B: By replacing traditional school subjects entirely with medicine
options.C: By banning young people from using mobile phones
options.D: By forcing all teenagers to visit a hospital every single month

explanation: Bringing services to schools and communities removes the travel and fear barriers that keep youths away from clinics. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which two main neurotransmitters are primarily used in the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Serotonin and dopamine
options.B: Acetylcholine and norepinephrine
options.C: Histamine and cortisol
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: These two chemicals are the principal messengers responsible for transmitting signals across autonomic nerve pathways. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T1#BMP124_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why must certain blood pressure medications like ACE inhibitors be stopped in early pregnancy?

options.A: They stop the placenta from attaching to the uterine wall
options.B: They cause immediate maternal kidney failure
options.C: They can cause severe birth defects in the developing fetus
options.D: They lower blood pressure far too quickly in the mother

explanation: ACE inhibitors can interfere with normal fetal growth and development, so midwives and doctors switch patients to safer alternatives. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T1#BMP221_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which physical sensation is most commonly reported by women experiencing early uterine prolapse?

options.A: A constant burning sensation during urination
options.B: Sudden numbness in both lower extremities
options.C: A heavy, dragging feeling in the pelvis
options.D: Sharp, stabbing pains in the lower back

explanation: The descent of the uterus pulls on supporting ligaments, creating a characteristic downward dragging or pressure sensation. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h3)

question: A midwife notices that a clinic frequently prescribes powerful antibiotics for mild post-procedure discomfort without signs of infection. Which principle of care is being violated?

options.A: Routine surgical asepsis
options.B: Emergency triage ranking
options.C: Antibiotic stewardship
options.D: Informed consent protocols

explanation: Antibiotic stewardship encourages careful and responsible prescribing to avoid creating resistant bacterial strains. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why is a chemical indicator strip placed inside an instrument pack before wrapping?

options.A: To show the patient that the hospital buys expensive supplies
options.B: To seal the wrapping paper securely shut during transit
options.C: To record the exact name of the midwife who packed the tray
options.D: To prove that the inside of the pack was exposed to sterilizing parameters

explanation: Internal indicators change color when exposed to specific temperatures and steam, confirming the sterilizing agent penetrated the pack. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is a primary socio-economic factor driving teenage pregnancy in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: High employment rates among young girls
options.B: Poverty and lack of financial resources
options.C: Excessive availability of free contraceptives
options.D: Mandatory sex education in primary schools

explanation: Poverty often leaves families and young girls desperate, sometimes resulting in early marriages or survival sex that increases the risk of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T2#BMP320_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is powdered infant formula considered a non-sterile food product?

options.A: The manufacturing process does not eliminate all bacterial spores present in the dry ingredients
options.B: Mothers usually touch the powder with unwashed hands inside their homes
options.C: The packaging containers are left open on shelves for long periods
options.D: Factories mix tap water directly into the tins during packaging

explanation: Using multiple drugs with different mechanisms ensures that any naturally resistant mutants are killed by the other agents in the regimen. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the standard daily therapeutic dose of zinc supplementation for a toddler who is eighteen months old?

options.A: 20 mg
options.B: 5 mg
options.C: 10 mg
options.D: 50 mg

explanation: Children between six months and five years of age receive 20 mg of elemental zinc daily during a diarrheal episode. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T3#BMP222_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which medicine used to prevent bleeding after birth should be avoided in a mother with severe high blood pressure?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Misoprostol
options.C: Ergometrine
options.D: Syntocinon

explanation: Ergometrine causes blood vessels to narrow, which can raise blood pressure to dangerous levels in women with hypertension. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h2)

question: When should a pregnant woman usually receive her first dose of preventive malaria treatment (IPTp-SP)?

options.A: Immediately upon confirming conception in the first week
options.B: Only during active labor in the delivery ward
options.C: Wait until the postpartum period after delivery
options.D: Early in the second trimester during routine antenatal care

explanation: IPTp-SP starts in the second trimester once the pregnancy is stable, and is continued at monthly intervals during clinic visits. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T4#BMP116_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why do many patients in primary health care clinics choose natural family planning?

options.A: They completely eliminate the risk of unintended pregnancy
options.B: They involve no financial cost or synthetic hormones
options.C: They guarantee complete protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: They require no daily tracking or physical observations

explanation: Natural methods appeal to many patients because they do not cost money and avoid chemical side effects. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h1)

question: A woman has weak contractions during the third stage of labor. Which hypothalamic hormone helps strengthen these contractions?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Vasopressin

explanation: Oxytocin is released from the back part of the pituitary gland and attaches to uterine muscle to help create strong contractions. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h2)

question: What happens when fibrous scar tissue squeezes the tiny blood vessels inside the liver?

options.A: Immediate overproduction of digestive enzymes
options.B: Rapid regeneration of healthy liver lobules
options.C: Sudden cooling of the core body temperature
options.D: Impaired blood circulation and restricted metabolic function

explanation: When scar tissue pinches these tiny blood vessels, blood flow slows down. Without good blood flow, liver cells miss out on vital oxygen and nutrients. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T2#BMP125_U4_T2_h2)

question: When is chemotherapy commonly administered in the treatment of malignant bone tumors?

options.A: Only after the patient has fully recovered from all surgeries
options.B: Before surgery to shrink the tumor or to target microscopic spread
options.C: As a quick pain reliever instead of standard analgesics
options.D: To replace the need for any diagnostic imaging or biopsy

explanation: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy helps shrink the primary tumor mass before surgical removal and kills stray cancer cells traveling in the body. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T5#BMP216_U3_T5_h6)

question: Over what timeframe do the questions on the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale ask the mother to reflect on her feelings?

options.A: The past seven days
options.B: The past six months
options.C: Since the day she discovered pregnancy
options.D: Throughout her entire childhood

explanation: The EPDS specifically directs mothers to report how they have felt during the previous week to capture recent mood states. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T2#BMP223_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do midwives use standard precautions for every single patient in the labour ward?

options.A: Hospital regulations require paperwork for every single birth.
options.B: It is impossible to wash hands without following standard rules.
options.C: Midwives only need protection when treating high-risk mothers.
options.D: Any patient can potentially carry and transmit infectious pathogens.

explanation: Standard precautions assume that body fluids from any person may contain infectious agents, so safety measures apply universally to protect both patients and healthcare workers. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h1)

question: How does the vomiting pattern in hyperemesis gravidarum differ from normal morning sickness?

options.A: It only happens immediately after drinking cold water
options.B: It stops completely by the tenth week of pregnancy
options.C: It occurs strictly during the early morning hours
options.D: It happens all day and night without relief

explanation: Unlike morning sickness which comes and goes, hyperemesis gravidarum involves unrelenting vomiting that persists throughout the entire day. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h4)

question: What does data backup involve in a computer system?

options.A: Installing a generator to prevent sudden power cuts in the clinic
options.B: Printing out physical paper copies of every single lab result
options.C: Making extra copies of electronic files and storing them safely elsewhere
options.D: Deleting old patient records to create more space on the hard drive

explanation: Backing up means duplicating important data so that a spare copy exists if the original is lost, stolen, or corrupted. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical sign or symptom of a molar pregnancy?

options.A: Passage of tissue vesicles resembling grapes
options.B: Uterine size much larger than expected for dates
options.C: Fetal kicking felt clearly at 10 weeks
options.D: Severe and persistent nausea and vomiting

explanation: Fetal movements cannot be felt at 10 weeks, especially in a molar pregnancy where normal fetal development is absent or severely compromised. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which action violates client confidentiality in a clinic?

options.A: Discussing a client's contraceptive choice in the waiting area
options.B: Closing the consultation room door during a private talk
options.C: Asking a client their preferred method behind a screen
options.D: Filing the client card securely inside the records cabinet

explanation: Private reproductive health choices must never be discussed where other clients or unauthorized staff can overhear them. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T4#BMP224_U1_T4_h3)

question: How does exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months help protect an infant from respiratory infections?

options.A: It creates an impermeable physical barrier inside the bronchial tubes
options.B: It increases the production of natural lung surfactant
options.C: It transfers protective maternal antibodies directly to the infant
options.D: It prevents the infant from ever coming into contact with cold viruses

explanation: Breast milk contains antibodies and immune factors that bolster an infant's developing immune system against common respiratory pathogens. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T10#BMP222_U2_T10_h8)

question: A client has vaginal dryness and pain during sex after menopause. What tissue change is causing this?

options.A: Atrophy of urogenital tissues due to low estrogen
options.B: Inflammation of the cervix caused by bacterial infection
options.C: Enlargement of the ovaries due to trapped fluid
options.D: Overgrowth of the uterine lining from high progesterone

explanation: Urogenital tissues need estrogen to stay thick and moist, so low estrogen levels lead to thinning and dryness. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T1#BMP320_U1_T1_h5)

question: How do facultative anaerobic bacteria behave when placed in a culture?

options.A: They will die immediately if any oxygen is introduced.
options.B: They can grow with or without oxygen present.
options.C: They strictly require high levels of carbon dioxide to multiply.
options.D: They only grow at extremely high temperatures above 60°C.

explanation: Facultative organisms are flexible, using oxygen when it is available but surviving without it when necessary. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T2#BMP116_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is pre-insertion counseling especially important in Nigerian midwifery practice?

options.A: To legally sign away the client's right to ask questions
options.B: To force the client to choose the most expensive device
options.C: To clear up local myths and prepare clients for bleeding changes
options.D: To prove that midwives know more about medicine than clients

explanation: Addressing common community fears and explaining normal side effects beforehand prevents unnecessary panic and premature removal of the device. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T8#BMP224_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary enzyme produced by Helicobacter pylori that helps it survive in acidic gastric juices?

options.A: Pepsin
options.B: Urease
options.C: Amylase
options.D: Lipase

explanation: Helicobacter pylori produces urease to break down urea into ammonia, creating a mild alkaline cloud around itself to neutralize stomach acid. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T5#BMP125_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT normally considered a disease-carrying vector in a clinical setting?

options.A: Houseflies
options.B: Earthworms
options.C: Cockroaches
options.D: Mosquitoes

explanation: Earthworms enrich soil and do not transmit human pathogens or act as disease vectors like flies, mosquitoes, or cockroaches. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T3#BMP117_U4_T3_h1)

question: In which year was the historic International Conference on Primary Health Care held at Alma-Ata?
explanation: The Alma-Ata Declaration was adopted at the international conference held in September 1978. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is a major problem with putting too much text on presentation slides?

options.A: It improves student retention of every single word
options.B: It automatically repairs damaged projection screens
options.C: It speeds up the overall delivery of the lecture
options.D: It causes cognitive overload for the learners

explanation: When slides are packed with text, students find it hard to read the screen and listen to the instructor at the same time. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h7)

question: What does the letter 'T' stand for in the GATHER counseling framework?

options.A: Tell the client about available contraceptive methods
options.B: Test the client for sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Train community health workers on pill distribution
options.D: Treat immediate side effects of hormonal drugs

explanation: In the GATHER acronym, T stands for telling or providing the client with clear information regarding the available family planning options. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T1#BMP224_U2_T1_h2)

question: When does classic vitamin K deficiency bleeding usually show up in a newborn?

options.A: At exactly fourteen days postpartum
options.B: Between two and seven days after birth
options.C: Between two weeks and six months of age
options.D: Within the first two hours of life

explanation: Classic vitamin K deficiency bleeding most commonly appears between the second and seventh day of life as mild bruising or oozing from the umbilical cord. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T1#BMP213_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is the lecture method not ideal for teaching practical midwifery skills like pelvic floor repair?

options.A: It is too expensive for nursing and midwifery schools to fund
options.B: It relies on passive listening rather than hands-on practice
options.C: It forces students to memorize complex chemical formulas
options.D: It requires advanced computers connected to the internet

explanation: Practical skills require physical demonstration and hands-on practice, which cannot be learned by listening to a lecture alone. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is a key feature of the chickenpox rash?

options.A: Large peeling sheets of skin on the chest
options.B: A rash starting only on the soles and palms
options.C: Lesions in different stages of development appearing all at once
options.D: All spots turning into hard dry scabs on the very first day

explanation: Chickenpox shows fresh bumps, fluid blisters, and dry scabs all on the skin at the same time. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T4#BMP222_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of a J-pouch procedure after a colectomy?

options.A: It preserves normal elimination through the rectum without a permanent bag
options.B: It allows the remaining colon tissue to regenerate new mucosal cells
options.C: It permanently eliminates the need for any follow-up blood tests
options.D: It speeds up the absorption of oral fats in the small intestine

explanation: The J-pouch is an internal reservoir made from the small bowel, letting patients pass stool normally through the anal canal without needing an external stoma bag. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T10#BMP125_U3_T10_h5)

question: What does the term Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause (GSM) describe?

options.A: A sudden surge of excess estrogen in late adulthood
options.B: A chronic spectrum of vulvar, vaginal, and urinary symptoms
options.C: An irreversible complete prolapse of the uterine corpus
options.D: A temporary acute viral infection of the pelvic organs

explanation: GSM is an umbrella term for the chronic changes and symptoms affecting the lower urinary and genital tracts during and after menopause. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T3#BMP320_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important to record the exact time and site of the vitamin K injection right away?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will never develop neonatal jaundice
options.B: It prevents accidental duplicate administration by oncoming shift staff
options.C: It satisfies legal requirements for surgical theatre documentation
options.D: It proves to the pharmaceutical company that the drug was effective

explanation: Clear charting ensures continuity of care and stops different healthcare workers from accidentally giving the baby a second dose. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T1#BMP213_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the specialized name for lipid-rich lymph that drains from the digestive tract?

options.A: Interstitial fluid
options.B: Chyle
options.C: Plasma
options.D: Serum

explanation: Chyle is the milky, fat-laden lymph collected from the lacteals in the small intestine during fat digestion. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h2)

question: Why is it important to ask a client about severe migraine headaches before prescribing a combined oral contraceptive?

options.A: Hormone pills stop headache medication from working properly
options.B: Headaches cause women to forget to swallow their daily pills
options.C: Estrogen cures chronic migraines and might mask other illnesses
options.D: Migraines with aura combined with estrogen increase the risk of stroke

explanation: Women who experience migraines with aura have a significantly higher risk of ischemic stroke when exposed to exogenous estrogen. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why must a midwife take an active interest in the community's environmental sanitation?

options.A: Maternal and child health outcomes depend heavily on clean surroundings
options.B: Hospital management requires midwives to clear outdoor gutters daily
options.C: Environmental officers cannot work without a qualified nurse present
options.D: It is the only way to prevent doctors from contracting malaria

explanation: A clean environment prevents infectious diseases that threaten the lives of mothers and newborns during pregnancy and after delivery. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T2#BMP117_U4_T2_h6)

question: How does emptying the fetal organs help in delivering the deceased baby?

options.A: It prevents amniotic fluid from entering the mother's bloodstream
options.B: It removes the rigid structure so the body can collapse and pass easily
options.C: It restarts the mother's heart rate to help her push
options.D: It dilates the maternal cervix to ten centimeters quickly

explanation: Without solid organs holding its shape, the fetal trunk easily flattens and slides through the birth canal. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T7#BMP311_U3_T7_h4)

question: When does ovulation actually happen in relation to the temperature rise on a BBT chart?

options.A: Just before the temperature climbs
options.B: Three days after the temperature rises
options.C: During the highest temperature peak of the cycle
options.D: Two weeks after the temperature rises

explanation: The temperature rises after ovulation due to progesterone, meaning ovulation usually happens right before the upward shift. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T4#BMP224_U4_T4_h3)

question: How does lignocaine stop pain signals from traveling along a nerve?

options.A: Stimulating local opioid receptors to block pain perception
options.B: Increasing potassium movement out of the cell completely
options.C: Destroying the myelin sheath surrounding the nerve fibre
options.D: Blocking sodium channels to prevent nerve depolarisation

explanation: Lignocaine works by blocking sodium channels, which stops the electrical signals the nerve needs to send pain messages to the brain. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T6#BMP213_U2_T6_h2)

question: A nurse is preparing to lift a heavy patient up in bed. How should the nurse protect their own trunk muscles?

options.A: Lean entirely backward while pulling the load.
options.B: Engage core stability and bend at the knees.
options.C: Use only arm strength without moving the feet.
options.D: Keep legs straight and twist quickly at the waist.

explanation: Bending the knees and bracing the core protects the spine from excessive shearing stress during heavy lifting tasks. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is an example of a hazard in a hospital emergency setting?

options.A: Spilled blood on the floor and broken glass
options.B: A calm patient resting quietly in bed
options.C: An empty and clean corridor
options.D: A properly locked drug cupboard

explanation: Biological fluids and sharp objects pose immediate physical and infection risks to anyone entering the area. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T8#BMP110_U7_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary ultrasound finding that confirms a complete abortion?

options.A: Multiple grape-like clusters filling the whole uterus
options.B: An empty uterine cavity with a thin endometrial lining
options.C: A gestational sac containing a live, active fetal heart
options.D: A thick mass of retained placental tissue and blood clots

explanation: An ultrasound showing an empty uterus with a thin lining proves that all products of conception have been expelled. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard responsibility of the midwife in reproductive cancer care?

options.A: Referring clients with suspicious lesions to specialists
options.B: Performing major surgical removal of ovarian tumours
options.C: Conducting visual inspection screening tests
options.D: Educating communities about risk factors

explanation: Major surgeries like tumour removals are performed by gynaecological surgeons, not midwives. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why are midwives well-positioned to spot early signs of child vulnerability in Nigeria?

options.A: Traditional rulers mandate that midwives inspect every household annually
options.B: Healthcare workers manage all social welfare payments distributed by the government
options.C: Midwives possess legal authority to prosecute abusive parents in local courts
options.D: Clinics provide regular contact with families during early childhood

explanation: Routine maternal and child health visits give healthcare workers repeated opportunities to observe family dynamics and home life. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T2#BMP222_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which physical sign on the nipple after a feed strongly suggests a poor, shallow latch?

options.A: Lipstick-shaped or creased appearance
options.B: Complete absence of skin moisture
options.C: Bright red coloration across the whole areola
options.D: Inverted shape pointing inward

question: Why might some community members hesitate to use digital health consultations?

options.A: Mobile phones are medically proven to cause pregnancy complications
options.B: Government policies strictly forbid the use of mobile phones for health
options.C: Midwives refuse to answer phone calls after normal working hours
options.D: They prefer traditional face-to-face interactions for sensitive health issues

explanation: Cultural reliance on physical presence and personal touch often breeds skepticism toward virtual healthcare. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which activity raises pressure inside the abdomen and increases the risk of a hernia?

options.A: Decreased daily fluid consumption
options.B: Elevated red blood cell count
options.C: Low resting systemic blood pressure
options.D: Straining during heavy lifting

explanation: Activities that force high pressure inside the abdomen push internal organs against vulnerable muscle walls. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T8#BMP125_U3_T8_h3)

question: What is the main way Hepatitis B passes from mother to baby during childbirth?

options.A: Transmission through casual touch in the clinic
options.B: Inhalation of respiratory droplets in the ward
options.C: Consuming poorly cooked meat during labor
options.D: Perinatal transmission from mother to baby

explanation: Babies can pick up the virus when they come into contact with maternal blood and body fluids while passing through the birth canal. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why might a postpartum mother complain of a pounding headache and dizziness shortly after receiving ergometrine?

options.A: The medication causes her body temperature to fall rapidly
options.B: The medicine makes her blood sugar drop to dangerous levels
options.C: The drug triggers an allergic skin rash across her face
options.D: The drug causes temporary elevation of systemic blood pressure

explanation: Widespread vasoconstriction raises blood pressure, which frequently manifests as a throbbing headache or dizziness. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T2#BMP213_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is immersing a newborn in unbathed basin water discouraged before the umbilical cord falls off?

options.A: Contaminated water can enter the open umbilical wound and introduce bacteria
options.B: Water makes the baby catch a cold more easily during the first week
options.C: Soaking dissolves the cord clamp before the vessels have closed
options.D: Wet skin prevents the mother from seeing the diaper area clearly

explanation: Sponge baths are recommended until the cord separates because immersing the unhealed navel in water increases the risk of bacterial contamination. [learn more](BMP214_U2_T3#BMP214_U2_T3_h5)

question: At 38 weeks, you feel no fetal head or breech in the lower abdomen. What should you do next?

options.A: Book her for a routine follow-up appointment in four weeks
options.B: Perform a digital vaginal examination to sweep the membranes
options.C: Arrange an urgent ultrasound scan and obstetric review
options.D: Advise the patient to walk around to encourage engagement

explanation: At 38 weeks, a transverse lie requires immediate investigation and specialist management, usually leading to a scheduled caesarean section. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T6#BMP311_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary danger of correcting high blood sodium too quickly with hypotonic fluids?

options.A: Permanent paralysis of the lower extremities
options.B: Rapid fluid shift into brain cells causing swelling
options.C: Sudden kidney failure from restricted blood flow
options.D: Severe high blood pressure and fluid in the lungs

explanation: Lowering blood sodium too fast causes water to rush into brain tissue, which swells and leads to dangerous neurological damage. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T4#BMP222_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main survival reason newborns have the rooting reflex?

options.A: Finding food and securing a breastfeeding latch
options.B: Strengthening the muscles of the neck and spine
options.C: Clearing mucus from the upper airway passages
options.D: Protecting the eyes from sudden bright lights

explanation: Turning toward a touch near the mouth helps the newborn find the breast or bottle for feeding easily. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T5#BMP214_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which ancient languages form the primary roots of most anatomical terms?

options.A: Arabic and Persian
options.B: Greek and Latin
options.C: French and Spanish
options.D: Igbo and Yoruba

explanation: Medical science traditionally builds its vocabulary from classic Greek and Latin word roots. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T1#BMP111_U1_T1_h1)

question: At approximately what gestational age do midwives routinely begin performing formal abdominal palpation maneuvers?

options.A: 24 weeks
options.B: 16 weeks
options.C: 36 weeks
options.D: 12 weeks

explanation: By 24 weeks of gestation, the uterus has grown well above the pelvis and fetal parts are large enough to be clearly distinguished through the abdominal wall. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h1)

question: A patient develops a pelvic infection two days after manual vacuum aspiration for an incomplete miscarriage. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Community-acquired viral exanthem from casual contact
options.B: Iatrogenic infection related to uterine instrumentation
options.C: Congenital infection passed down from the mother
options.D: Spontaneous hormonal infection unrelated to the procedure

explanation: Procedures that cross the cervical barrier into the uterus frequently introduce bacteria, leading to iatrogenic complications. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h2)

question: A pregnant woman eats a meal of beans and spinach. Which food item should a midwife suggest she consume alongside this meal to greatly improve iron absorption?

options.A: Strong local black tea without milk
options.B: Fresh orange juice containing vitamin C
options.C: Unrefined sorghum with high phytate levels
options.D: Cold whole cow's milk high in calcium

explanation: Vitamin C significantly enhances the absorption of non-heme plant iron in the gut, whereas tea, phytates, and calcium can inhibit it. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T9#BMP118_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which sugar is found in the highest amount in human breast milk?

options.A: Lactose
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Fructose
options.D: Sucrose

explanation: Lactose is the primary sugar in human milk, giving the baby energy and helping brain development. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T1#BMP214_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is a major advantage shared by both male and female condoms?

options.A: They provide protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They completely eliminate the risk of accidental pregnancy
options.C: They require a doctor's prescription
options.D: They can be washed and reused multiple times

explanation: Both methods act as physical shields that help stop the spread of infections like HIV and gonorrhea. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T1#BMP224_U3_T1_h5)

question: What main body function changes in a newborn that affects how medications leave their body?

options.A: Increased gastric acidity
options.B: Decreased total body fat
options.C: Elevated liver enzyme production
options.D: Changes in how the kidneys clear substances

explanation: Kidney function develops quickly after birth, which changes how the newborn filters and clears medications from the body. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which pressure injury stage shows intact skin with redness that does not turn white when pressed?

options.A: Stage 3
options.B: Stage 4
options.C: Stage 1
options.D: Stage 2

explanation: Stage 1 is the earliest visible sign of tissue stress, showing persistent redness that does not turn white when pressed. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T6#BMP110_U5_T6_h3)

question: What causes normal skin changes like spider veins and red palms during pregnancy?

options.A: Low circulating cortisol
options.B: Elevated estrogen levels
options.C: Deficiencies in dietary iron
options.D: High parathyroid activity

explanation: High estrogen causes blood vessels to dilate, leading to harmless skin signs like spider angiomas and red palms. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T8#BMP212_U1_T8_h7)

question: A midwife is getting ready to repair a tear after birth. What is the main infection control goal?

options.A: Reducing the total volume of blood loss from the placental site
options.B: Ensuring the mother remains fully awake throughout the entire suturing process
options.C: Speeding up the uterine involution process in the immediate postpartum period
options.D: Preventing introduction of bacteria into the open perineal wound layers

explanation: Stitching creates a healing wound where introduced bacteria can multiply and cause localized infection or wound breakdown. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common local side effect of using spermicide repeatedly?

options.A: Allergic contact dermatitis
options.B: Local tissue irritation
options.C: Permanent stopping of ovulation
options.D: Vaginal burning or itching

explanation: Spermicides act locally in the vagina and do not suppress ovarian function or alter body hormone levels. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T3#BMP224_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why are vaginal yeast infections generally not classed as classic sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: It only occurs when a patient has a completely destroyed immune system.
options.B: It only affects women who have never engaged in any form of sexual intercourse.
options.C: It cannot be found in male partners under any clinical circumstances.
options.D: It arises mainly from an overgrowth of fungi already present in the normal vaginal flora.

explanation: Yeast infections usually result from an internal imbalance of normal vaginal microbes rather than being strictly passed through sexual contact. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a core right of family planning clients?

options.A: Right to forced compliance with community norms
options.B: Right to complete and accurate health information
options.C: Right to privacy regarding personal medical details
options.D: Right to safe and accessible clinical services

explanation: Clients have rights to autonomy and choice, meaning they are never required to follow community pressure or force. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T5#BMP224_U1_T5_h2)

question: A midwife wants to assess a shy postnatal mother for anxiety during a clinic visit. What is the best approach?

options.A: Wait until the woman brings up her mental health on her own
options.B: Tell the woman that worrying is a waste of time and move on
